screen: Task Management — Reports & Analysis + Administration (Status, Priority, Permissions, Integrations, Audit Logs)
screenLevelGaps: ALL SIX FILES EXIST and were read in full (246 / 224 / 209 / 117 / 110 / 167 lines). None is mock-data — every one calls a real Laravel endpoint. The customer's blanket suspicion that these screens are fake is WRONG; the defects are narrower and are listed below.

VERDICT on 'are statuses/priorities actually consumed by the task board?' — STATUSES: YES. TaskOptionSetService::resolveStatus() is called by WorkspaceController.php:245 and MyTasksController.php:188 on every status write, task-workspace.tsx:120-121 builds the board's status filter from filters.status_options, and my-task-details-drawer.tsx:86-92 offers custom statuses in the executor's status picker. PRIORITIES: NO — this half is broken. WorkspaceController.php:150 returns filters.priority_options and task-workspace.tsx:66 reads ONLY response.data.filters.status_options, discarding priority_options. create-task-modal.tsx:535 hardcodes (['High','Medium','Low'] as const), typed at :71 as 'High'|'Medium'|'Low'. task-workspace.tsx:231 hardcodes ['High','Medium','Low'] for the Priority Distribution chart. There is no priority filter control anywhere in the workspace toolbar at all. NET: an admin can create a custom priority 'Urgent' (the customer's own spec, TaskManagementFeatures.txt Admin bullet 1, names Urgent explicitly), the API will accept it on a write, and NO SCREEN WILL EVER OFFER IT. Priority Management is a write-only screen.

VERDICT on 'Is Permission real server-side enforcement or UI only?' — The ENFORCEMENT is real, the SCREEN is decorative. TaskPermissionMiddleware.php exists, is aliased in bootstrap/app.php:34, and is attached to ~35 write routes in routes/api.php:869-955. So it is NOT UI-only theatre. BUT: (a) the rule is binary — TaskPermissionMiddleware.php:31-40 PRIVILEGED list vs a single strcasecmp against the literal string 'Employee' at :78 — so EVERY non-Employee profile (Admin, HR, Manager, Executive, Dept Head, whatever a tenant seeds) gets an IDENTICAL all-true column; a 6-profile tenant sees 6 identical columns of green ticks; (b) the screen is deliberately read-only (tm-permissions.tsx:11-13 admits it), so the customer's spec item 'Assign roles, manage data visibility constraints, and configure access policies' is 0% implemented; (c) FAIL-OPEN BUG: TaskPermissionMiddleware.php:69-71 returns false (=not an employee =privileged) when user_profile_id is 0/null, so any user with no profile assigned gets full delete/approve/admin rights; (d) TENANT-RENAME BUG: the check is on the literal profile NAME 'Employee'; a corporate customer who calls the role 'Associate', 'Staff' or 'Team Member' silently grants everyone destructive rights — a hard blocker for 'sale to corporate customers across many industries'.

VERDICT on 'What does Integration integrate with?' — Three read-only cards, and the screen materially MISREPRESENTS the backend. (1) n8n: config/services.php:31-36 is real, and LegacyTaskController.php:183-197 fires it — but NO FRONTEND CODE CALLS /task-management/legacy-tasks (grep across g2gv0 returns zero hits). create-task-modal.tsx creates tasks via services/task/index.ts:522 webClient.postForm('/task?...') → front_desk/taskController@store, which never calls fireWebhook. So the card's claim 'Notifies an n8n workflow whenever a task is created through the API' is FALSE for the app's actual create path. (2) UNDISCLOSED HARDCODED EXFILTRATION: front_desk/taskController.php:916 posts the ENTIRE task row ($updatedTask->toArray(), plus sub_institute_id) to the literal URL https://dev.triz.co.in/webhook/449cab91-32ac-4c27-ab77-b6a9389185c4 on every task UPDATE, with no config check and no opt-out — and this IS the live path (services/task/index.ts:545 webClient.putForm('/task/{id}')). It is not on the Integrations screen, so the page's promise 'Configured server-side via environment variables' is untrue. Every corporate tenant's task data goes to the vendor's dev server. (3) FCM card is measuring the wrong thing: SessionController.php:138 tests env('FCM_SERVER_KEY'), but FCM_SERVER_KEY is read NOWHERE ELSE in hp_erp; the real implementation (front_desk/taskController.php:187 and BulkTaskController.php:516-529) uses kreait/firebase-php with a service-account JSON hardcoded to storage_path('app/firebase/gapstogrowth-ba988-firebase-adminsdk-fbsvc.json') — the vendor's own Firebase project. Setting FCM_SERVER_KEY has zero effect; not setting it does not disable push. Additionally env() outside a config file returns null once php artisan config:cache runs, so in production this card ALWAYS reads 'Not configured'. (4) config/services.php:43-48 defines a Slack integration that the screen does not surface (nothing consumes it either). (5) The customer spec asks for 'version control systems, communication channels, CRM pipelines... and automate data ingestion' — none of the three is any of those, and there is no Connect / Test / Disconnect / ingest action on the page.

REPORTS DEFECT #1 (the customer is RIGHT, and this is the worst one): the Delays tab's 'On Hold, by reason' panel can only ever show one row, 'Uncategorised'. ReportController.php:75 groups by task.delay_category. The ONLY writer of delay_category in the whole backend is MyTasksController.php:205, which only writes it if the request body contains delay_category. services/task/index.ts:266-269 updateMyTaskStatus sends exactly {token, sub_institute_id, syear, status, remarks} — delay_category is never sent. my-task-details-drawer.tsx has no delay-category picker (line 23 offers 'On Hold' as a bare status). WorkspaceController.php:346-356 also drives tasks to ON HOLD on reject without setting delay_category. So the column is never populated and COALESCE(delay_category,'Uncategorised') at ReportController.php:75 always wins. This simultaneously kills the customer's Employee spec bullet 'Blocker Flagging: ...document the specific operational hurdles preventing execution to alert their Department Head.'

REPORTS DEFECT #2: the Learning Recommendations tab is scoped to the wrong person AND joins the wrong ID space. tm-reports.tsx:58 calls getRejectedTaskLearning(context) with no userId; services/task/index.ts:249 defaults user_id to context.userId — the LOGGED-IN ADMIN. So on a page headed 'Org-wide task performance' (tm-reports.tsx:87) the third tab silently shows only the admin's own rejected work. Worse, SkillMatchingController.php:246 does whereIn('ssm.subject_id', $allSkillIds) where $allSkillIds come from task.skill_id — and task.skill_id holds s_users_skills.id (UserSkillController.php:96-100), while sub_std_map.subject_id is a foreign key to the `subject` table (2025_06_02_093430_create_sub_std_map_table.php:41-44). Two unrelated ID namespaces. Matches are coincidental. The SIBLING endpoint /user-rejected-tasks (SkillMatchingController.php:19-199) does this correctly — it resolves skill titles and matches sub_std_map.display_name by name, falling back to subject_id only as a last resort — and the frontend calls the WRONG one of the two.

REPORTS DEFECT #3: tm-reports.tsx:57-64 swallows EVERY failure of the learning endpoint into the single sentence 'No rejected tasks — no learning recommendations right now.' SkillMatchingController returns 404 for 'No rejected tasks', 404 for 'No course found for these skills', 400 for 'No skills found in rejected tasks', and 500 on exception. A database outage, a tenant with no course catalogue, and a genuinely clean employee are all reported to the admin as the same reassuring message. A report that reports 'nothing wrong' when it has actually failed is worse than a report that errors.

REPORTS DEFECT #4: tm-reports.tsx:48-51 uses Promise.all for productivity+delays, and :65-66 sets a single `error`. The render guards at :114, :149 and :187 are all `!loading && !error`. One failing endpoint blanks all three tabs, including the one that succeeded.

REPORTS DEFECT #5 — the Task→LMS hand-off is a dead end, and the missing pieces already exist in the backend. The full chain is built: (1) recommend = /user-rejected-tasks-courses [wired]; (2) persist the suggestion = POST /api/employee/course-suggestions, SuggestedCourseController.php:15-48, routed at routes/api.php:855, takes exactly {employee_id, task_id, course_id, course_name} [NOT wired — zero frontend callers]; (3) learner reads suggestions = lms_apiController::getSuggestedCoursesByUser at :765 [NOT EVEN ROUTED — no entry in routes/api.php]; (4) enrol = POST /api/enroll, routes/api.php:756 [not wired from here]. The Learning tab renders read-only cards with no Assign, no Enrol, no 'suggest to employee' action (tm-reports.tsx:236-242 is a plain div). The ownership model says LMS BUILDS skill and Task Management is EXECUTION evidence; the evidence is computed and then thrown away.

REPORTS DEFECT #6 — the reports have no HR/competency dimension at all. The customer's HR Manager spec asks for 'Competency Identification: Map task performance and execution speeds against specific roles to identify functional skill gaps or emerging internal subject matter experts.' ReportController::productivity (:30-45) groups ONLY by task_allocated_to and joins ONLY tbluser. It never touches task.skill_id, task.required_skills, tbluser.allocated_standards (job role), s_skill_matrix or hrms_departments. There is no department column, no job-role column, no skill column, no filter for any of them. Nothing in this module ever writes back to s_skill_matrix (consistent with the known ground truth), so applied-capability evidence never reaches Competency.

REPORTS DEFECT #7 — no time dimension anywhere. Both reports are point-in-time snapshots: ReportController has no from/to parameters and the UI exposes no date range. The Executive spec asks for 'organizational velocity' and 'bottleneck alerts'; you cannot compute a trend or an alert from a single snapshot. There is also no Export on Reports (Audit Logs has one), no refresh control (tm-reports.tsx:70 useCallback has an empty dep array, so the only way to refetch is a full page reload), and no sorting despite the file's own docblock at :7-8 claiming the productivity view is 'sortable at a glance'.

API AUTHORISATION GAP: every GET in the task-management group is UNGATED. routes/api.php:895-896 declares /reports/productivity and /reports/delays with no task.permission middleware; the same is true of /statuses, /priorities, /integrations, /permissions and /workspace. Only /audit-logs and /audit-logs/export carry a gate (routes/api.php:900-901). Any employee holding a valid Sanctum token can curl the org-wide productivity table of every colleague, and can enumerate the tenant's full profile list via /permissions. UI menu rights (tblmenumaster_g2g) hide the screen; they do not protect the endpoint.

AUDIT LOG GAP: AuditLogController.php:112-126 supports task_id, actor_id, event, from and to filters, and services/task/index.ts:160-171 already passes them through. tm-audit-logs.tsx wires NONE of them — the only control is a free-text box (:106-111) that filters client-side over the 50 rows of the current page (:70-74). An admin searching for a task that sits on page 7 is told 'Nothing on this page matches the filter' (:122). Export CSV (:99) calls auditLogsExportUrl(context) which passes no filters at all (services/task/index.ts:173-176), so the export ignores whatever the admin just typed and always dumps up to 10 000 rows.

AUDIT LOG COVERAGE GAP: EVENT_LABELS at tm-audit-logs.tsx:23-32 covers 8 slugs. The backend emits at least 23 (grep of taskChanged/configChanged call sites): created, updated, legacy_updated, legacy_deleted, workspace_updated, status_changed, archived, approved, rejected, deadline_extended, schedule_updated, subtask_added, subtask_completed, subtask_reopened, subtask_removed, timer_started, timer_stopped, status_created, status_updated, status_deactivated, priority_created, priority_updated, priority_deactivated. The 15 unmapped ones render raw at :133 as e.g. 'subtask_reopened' and 'priority_deactivated'. Config events also carry task_id 0 (TaskAuditService.php:86), so they render a meaningless '#0' badge at tm-audit-logs.tsx:148.

AUDIT LOG FIDELITY GAP: TaskAuditService.php:42-50 snapshots ONLY status, task_allocated_to, task_date, approve_status and a free-text detail — and NEVER the after-state. So a 'Task edited' row cannot tell you what the title, description, priority, owner or remarks changed FROM or TO; a 'Status changed' row shows the old status only. For the customer's stated purpose ('comprehensive system logs to track task creation, deletion, or critical modifications for compliance and security auditing') a before-only, five-field diff is not a compliance trail.

STATUS/PRIORITY MANAGEMENT — 'reorder' and 'colour' are advertised and absent. tm-status-management.tsx:8-9 says custom statuses are 'created, renamed, re-ordered and deactivated here'; tm-priority-management.tsx:8-9 says 'ordered (lower sorts first)'. Neither form has a sort_order input (status form = name + category only, :143-155; priority form = name + SLA only, :129-148), so save() at :96-97 / :82-83 never sends sort_order and every custom row is inserted at the hardcoded default 50 (TaskOptionController.php:75 and :224). Ordering is therefore whatever insertion order MySQL returns after the usort at TaskOptionSetService.php:56/:83. Likewise TaskStatusOption.color exists in the type (types/task-management.ts:127), in the API (TaskOptionController.php:74) and in the DB, and there is no colour control in the UI and no consumer — StatusBadge (components/ui/status-badge.tsx) has no colour prop at all.

STATUS/PRIORITY MANAGEMENT — DEACTIVATION IS IRREVERSIBLE FROM THE UI. The Deactivate button is rendered only when option.active is true (tm-status-management.tsx:211, tm-priority-management.tsx:196). The Edit form contains no active toggle, and save() sends only {name, category} / {name, sla_hours} — so TaskOptionController.php:131 `$request->boolean('active', (bool) $row->active)` preserves the false. There is no Reactivate control. An admin who deactivates 'In Review' by mistake has no path back through the product; the row can only be revived with direct SQL.

STATUS MANAGEMENT — a custom status gets no board column of its own. The customer's spec asks for statuses like 'To Do, In Progress, Review, Blocked, Done'. TaskOptionSetService::resolveStatus (:97-116) collapses every custom name onto one of four system categories, and task-workspace.tsx:165-171 hardcodes its five Grid columns off task.status + task.approved. So a tenant that creates 'Review' sees those tasks filed under whichever category they mapped to; the label appears only as badge text (task-workspace.tsx:27-29). This is a defensible architecture, but it means 'custom task statuses' is a labelling feature, not a workflow feature, and nothing on screen says so.

PERMISSIONS — /task-management/permissions is itself ungated (routes/api.php:865), and SessionController.php:65-72 applies ->unique() to profile NAMES after ordering by sort_order; two tenant profiles sharing a name silently collapse into one column.

AUDIT EXPORT — tm-audit-logs.tsx:81 sets link.href = taskService.auditLogsExportUrl(context), and services/task/index.ts:173-176 puts the live Sanctum token in the query string. services/core/api-client.ts:9-22 documents at length why that is unacceptable ('a token harvested from a log is a working credential'). The download necessarily cannot carry a header, so this needs a short-lived signed download URL; today the admin's session token lands in browser history and every proxy log. If the export 403s (Employee profile), the anchor click just downloads a JSON error body — tm-audit-logs.tsx:76-83 has no response handling.

CROSS-CHECK, customer suspicion partially WRONG: the transition matrix shown on the Status screen (tm-status-management.tsx:27-32) is an EXACT match for the rule the server enforces (TaskStatusTransitionService.php:16-22). It is accurate today. It is however a hand-maintained duplicate — the /statuses response already carries `categories` (TaskOptionController.php:44) which the component ignores, and the transition matrix is not exposed by any endpoint, so this will drift the moment the server rule changes.

features.purpose: Create or update a custom status
features.shouldFeed: Audit Logs (it does — TaskOptionController.php:81 and :144 call configChanged)
features.gap: Genuinely writes and genuinely audits. But save() at :92 calls getLaravelContext() without the isLaravelContextReady guard that load() uses at :55, so an expired session produces a bare 401 instead of the friendly 'Please sign in again'.

For a CUSTOM status the badge deliberately shows its CATEGORY, so a row can read badge 'ON HOLD' directly beside the bold name 'In Review'. option.color is fetched (types/task-management.ts:127) and never used — components/ui/status-badge.tsx has no colour prop at all.

features.purpose: Identify the status and its active state
features.gap: Inactive rows are returned because the controller calls statuses($sid, false) (TaskOptionController.php:43) while every consumer calls it with activeOnly=true — correct, so an admin sees deactivated rows that users no longer see.

features.element: Status list — system row 'Can move to:' transition chips
features.shouldFeed: Should mirror TaskStatusTransitionService, which is what the server enforces
features.gap: VERIFIED ACCURATE today — an exact match for TaskStatusTransitionService.php:16-22. But it is a hand-copied duplicate: no endpoint exposes the matrix, so any change to the server rule silently makes this screen lie. Also, custom statuses show no transition information at all (:198 just says 'Behaves as X'), even though they inherit their category's rules.

Correctly enforced server-side too: system statuses are code constants (TaskOptionSetService.php:20-25) with id null, and their names are reserved by statusNameTaken (TaskOptionController.php:338-342).

features.purpose: Load a custom status into the form
features.gap: Renders for inactive rows too, but the resulting save cannot reactivate them (no `active` field is sent) — see next entry.

features.purpose: Retire a custom status without breaking existing tasks
features.shouldFeed: All status pickers should stop offering it (they do — resolveStatus filters active=true at TaskOptionSetService.php:109)
features.gap: Soft-delete works and is audited. But it is a ONE-WAY DOOR in the product: the button is hidden once active is false (:211), the Edit form has no active toggle, and save() sends only {name, category} so TaskOptionController.php:131 preserves active=false. There is no Reactivate control anywhere. Also uses window.confirm rather than the app's dialog components.

features.element: MISSING: sort_order input on the status form
features.purpose: Control display order of custom statuses
features.shouldFeed: The order of every status dropdown in the module
features.gap: The API accepts it (TaskOptionController.php:59, :75), the service signature declares it (services/task/index.ts:196), the type declares it (types/task-management.ts:128) — and there is no control, so every custom status is created at the hardcoded default 50. The file's own docblock at :8 says statuses are 're-ordered ... here'.

features.element: MISSING: colour picker on the status form
features.shouldFeed: StatusBadge across the board, list, calendar and drawer
features.gap: Column, validation (TaskOptionController.php:58) and type all exist; no control and no renderer consumes it.

features.element: MISSING: 'in use by N tasks' indicator
features.purpose: Warn before deactivating a heavily used status
features.gap: The confirm dialog claims tasks keep the label but gives no count. An admin cannot tell whether they are retiring a label used by 2 tasks or 2000.

features.element: Priority subtitle 'validated on every task write the moment they exist. SLA hours are informational for now.'
features.gap: Half true and materially misleading. 'Validated on every task write' is true (WorkspaceController.php:250, LegacyTaskController.php:145) — but validation is not availability: no screen ever OFFERS a custom priority, so a custom level can only ever be applied by a hand-crafted API call. The SLA caveat is honest but understates it: sla_hours has no reader at all in either repo.

features.shouldFeed: The priority picker in create-task-modal, the workspace priority filter, and the Priority Distribution chart
features.gap: Writes correctly and rename cascades to task.task_type (TaskOptionController.php:284-289), but nothing consumes the result. create-task-modal.tsx:535 and :71 hardcode High/Medium/Low; task-workspace.tsx:231 hardcodes them for the chart; task-workspace.tsx discards filters.priority_options at :66. Creating 'Urgent' — the customer's own example — produces an unreachable row.

features.purpose: Attach a service-level target to a priority
features.shouldFeed: Overdue/breach computation in the Delays report, escalation alerts, and the Department Head's 'ensure SLAs are met' spec bullet
features.gap: Stored and never read. Grep of both repos: sla_hours appears only in this component, the service payload types, the type definition and the controller's INSERT/UPDATE. ReportController computes overdue purely from task_date; nothing anywhere compares elapsed time against sla_hours. This is a data-entry field with no downstream effect.

features.purpose: Create or update a custom priority
features.shouldFeed: Audit Logs (it does) and all priority pickers (it does not)
features.gap: The write and the audit are real; the consumption is not. Also note the empty-string quirk at :79 — clearing the SLA field on an EDIT omits sla_hours from the payload, and TaskOptionController.php:278 then defaults to the existing row value, so an SLA can be set but never cleared.

features.element: Priority list — ShieldAlert icon per row
features.gap: Identical icon on every row regardless of severity — carries no information.

features.reads: option.name lowercased against a 5-key style map
features.gap: The style map (priority-badge.tsx:3-9) knows low/medium/high/critical/urgent. Any other custom name falls through to neutral grey (:16). There is no colour field on task_management_priorities at all, so a tenant naming a level 'P0' or 'Blocker' gets an uncoloured chip with no remedy.

features.purpose: Identify the level and its state

features.gap: Displays a number that governs nothing. System priorities always render 'No SLA' because TaskOptionSetService.php:79 hardcodes sla_hours null for High/Medium/Low and they cannot be edited — so the three levels 99% of tasks actually use can never carry an SLA.
Enforced server-side: names reserved at TaskOptionController.php:352-356, rows are code constants at TaskOptionSetService.php:27-31.

features.purpose: Load a custom priority into the form

features.shouldFeed: All priority pickers should stop offering it
features.gap: Same one-way door as statuses — no Reactivate path in the UI. And since no picker ever offered the priority in the first place, deactivating it changes nothing visible.

features.element: MISSING: sort_order input on the priority form
features.purpose: Order custom levels relative to High/Medium/Low
features.shouldFeed: The order of priority dropdowns and the severity ordering used for escalation
features.gap: Docblock at :8-9 says levels are 'ordered (lower sorts first)' here. There is no control; everything lands at 50, i.e. after Low (30). A custom 'Urgent' therefore sorts BELOW 'Low' in TaskOptionSetService's merged list — the exact opposite of its severity.

features.element: Server-supplied note 'Enforced server-side by task.permission middleware; the Employee profile is denied privileged abilities.'
features.purpose: Tell the admin what the matrix means
features.gap: Literally accurate. It also inadvertently discloses the whole security model: the ONLY thing that grants privilege is not being named 'Employee'.

features.element: Matrix profile column headers (one per tbluserprofilemaster row)
features.reads: tbluserprofilemaster WHERE sub_institute_id AND status=1 AND deleted_at IS NULL ORDER BY sort_order, pluck(name)->unique()
features.shouldFeed: Organization/HRIT owns the profile master; the task module correctly treats it as the source of truth
features.gap: Correct source, but ->unique() on the NAME collapses two distinct profiles that share a name into one column, and the grid width is inline-computed at :75 with no horizontal scroll container — a tenant with 8+ profiles gets crushed columns on a laptop.
Non-privileged, so every profile shows a tick. Column is uniform.

The matrix shows a flat tick for everyone, which is misleading: the REAL restriction is ownership-scoped inside WorkspaceController::canEditTask (:502-513) — an Employee may only edit tasks they own/created/are assigned. That nuance is invisible on the matrix, so the screen under-reports the actual policy.

features.purpose: Show who may move a task

features.reads: privileged=true → false only for a profile literally named 'Employee'
features.gap: Enforced, but by TaskPermissionMiddleware.php:78 strcasecmp against the literal 'Employee'. A tenant using any other name for their base role grants delete to everyone, and the matrix will confidently render ticks confirming it.

features.element: Ability row 'Approve / reject completed work' (task.approve) — PRIVILEGED
features.purpose: Show who may sign off deliverables
features.gap: The customer's spec puts sign-off with the Department Head, i.e. the task OWNER. The middleware grants it to every non-Employee profile in the tenant regardless of whether they own the task — WorkspaceController::approve (:312-364) performs no ownership check at all, only a COMPLETED-status check. Any HR user can approve any department's deliverables.

features.purpose: Show who may edit/archive projects and membership
Show who may wire task dependencies
features.shouldFeed: routes/api.php:944-946; the customer's Dept-Head 'Cross-Departmental Dependencies' bullet

features.gap: The LABEL is wrong and hides real authority. notification.manage is the ability that also gates Status CRUD (routes/api.php:870-877), Priority CRUD, session revocation (:878) and — critically — reading and exporting the entire org-wide AUDIT LOG (:900-901). An admin reading this matrix has no way to know that ticking 'Manage notifications' for a profile hands them the compliance trail.

features.element: Allowed / denied cell (tick or cross with title tooltip)
features.purpose: State whether a profile has an ability
features.gap: Not interactive — no checkbox, no onClick, no keyboard target; the tooltip at :98 is the only affordance. Because privilege is binary, every non-Employee column is byte-identical, so a 5-profile tenant sees 5 identical columns of ticks and learns nothing about their role design.

features.element: MISSING: Save / edit controls on the permission matrix
features.api: NONE — no PUT/POST permissions endpoint exists in routes/api.php
features.shouldFeed: Every task write route; and Organization/HRIT, which owns roles
features.gap: The customer's Admin spec bullet 2 is 'Assign roles, manage data visibility constraints, and configure access policies determining who can see or modify tasks across departments.' None of assign / manage-visibility / configure-policy exists, in the UI or the API. The component's docblock (:11-13) is candid that per-tenant permission editing 'needs a storage decision first' — i.e. this is a known unbuilt feature, not a bug.

features.purpose: Control who sees tasks outside their department
features.shouldFeed: WorkspaceController scoping; Organization/HRIT hierarchy is the source of truth for department and reporting line
features.gap: Visibility is hardcoded in WorkspaceController's scope handling (all|mine|created|team|department) with no tenant configuration, and the 'all' scope is available to anyone with a token. There is no policy surface at all.

features.element: Integrations subtitle 'Configured server-side via environment variables. Keys are never shown here.'
features.gap: False as a description of the system. front_desk/taskController.php:916 fires a HARDCODED webhook to https://dev.triz.co.in/... on every task update, configured by nothing and disclosed nowhere; and the real FCM credential is a service-account JSON file, not an env var.

features.purpose: Report whether the n8n outbound webhook is configured
features.shouldFeed: Task creation should notify the configured automation endpoint
features.gap: The env check is honest but the DESCRIPTION is not: the only caller of fireWebhook is LegacyTaskController.php:183, and no frontend code calls /task-management/legacy-tasks (zero grep hits in g2gv0). The app's real create path is webClient.postForm('/task?...') → front_desk/taskController@store, which never fires it. So configuring N8N_TASK_WEBHOOK_URL produces no webhook for tasks created in the product.

features.element: Integration card — Gemini AI task generation
features.gap: The most honest of the three: config/gemini.php:17 reads GEMINI_API_KEY and create-task-modal.tsx calls generateTaskDetails → /gemini_chat (services/task/index.ts:657). One caveat: the card is tenant-agnostic — every customer shares whatever key is in the vendor's .env, with no per-tenant key and no usage metering.

The status indicator is measuring a variable nothing consumes. FCM_SERVER_KEY appears in exactly one place in hp_erp — this check. The working implementation (front_desk/taskController.php:187, BulkTaskController.php:516-529) uses kreait/firebase-php against storage_path('app/firebase/gapstogrowth-ba988-firebase-adminsdk-fbsvc.json'), a hardcoded path naming the vendor's own Firebase project. So: setting the advertised env var does nothing, not setting it does not disable push, and every corporate tenant's push traffic routes through one shared vendor Firebase project. Additionally env() outside a config file returns null under php artisan config:cache, so in a cached production build this card is permanently stuck on 'Not configured'.

Reports presence of a config value, never reachability. There is no health check, no last-delivery timestamp, no failure count — even though LegacyTaskController.php:197 already logs task.n8n_webhook_failed. An admin cannot distinguish 'configured and working' from 'configured and failing every call'.

features.element: Integration card — env var name in a <code> footer
features.purpose: Tell the admin which variable to set
features.gap: Correct for n8n and Gemini; actively wrong for FCM, where it instructs the admin to set FCM_SERVER_KEY, which nothing reads.
Same generic icon for all three; Gemini and FCM are not webhooks.

features.purpose: Manage an integration from the product
features.gap: The card grid is entirely read-only. The docblock (:12-14) defends this for secrets, which is reasonable — but a Test-connection button leaks no secret and is the single most useful control on this screen. There is no inbound webhook / ingestion surface either, which the customer's spec explicitly asks for ('automate data ingestion').

features.element: MISSING: the hardcoded dev.triz.co.in outbound webhook is not listed
features.writes: POSTs the full task row to a fixed third-party URL on every task update
features.shouldFeed: Should be a configurable, disclosed integration like the n8n card
features.gap: Highest-severity finding on this screen. Every tenant's task rows (title, description, assignee, remarks, sub_institute_id) are POSTed to the vendor's dev n8n instance on every update via the live PUT /task/{id} path, unconditionally, with the failure silently swallowed (:924-927, the log line is commented out). Not configurable, not disclosed, not disableable. A blocker for any corporate sale with a data-processing agreement.

features.purpose: Surface the Slack config that already exists
features.shouldFeed: The customer's spec asks explicitly for 'communication channels'
features.gap: config/services.php defines slack.notifications.bot_user_oauth_token and channel; grep shows nothing in app/ reads them. Dead config, and the one integration the customer named that the screen could plausibly have shown.

features.element: Audit Logs subtitle 'Every task change, who made it, and what it looked like before.'
features.gap: 'Every task change' overstates it — the snapshot is five fields (TaskAuditService.php:42-50), so title/description/priority/owner edits produce a row that records none of what changed. And there is no after-state at all.

Streams real data with CSV-injection neutralisation (AuditLogController.php:92-99) — genuinely well built server-side. Client-side it has four defects: (1) auditLogsExportUrl passes NO filters (services/task/index.ts:173-176), so the export ignores the search box and any implied scope; (2) the live Sanctum token is embedded in the href query string, which the app's own api-client.ts:9-22 documents as unacceptable; (3) the disabled guard uses logs.length (the current page) while the export covers all pages; (4) a 403 or 500 downloads a JSON error body as 'task-audit-logs.csv' with no handling.

features.element: Free-text filter input 'Filter by task, person, or event…'
features.reads: the 50 rows of the current page
features.shouldFeed: Should drive the server-side task_id/event/actor filters the API already supports
features.gap: Filters only the loaded page. AuditLogController.php:112-126 supports task_id, actor_id, event, from and to, and services/task/index.ts:160-171 already forwards all of them — none is wired. An admin searching a task on page 7 gets 'Nothing on this page matches the filter' (:122). Also case-insensitive substring only, no debounce, no clear button.

features.purpose: Show only approvals, or only deletions
features.shouldFeed: Compliance review of 'task creation, deletion, or critical modifications' — the customer's exact words
features.gap: Server-side filter exists (AuditLogController.php:118-120) and the service parameter exists (services/task/index.ts:166); no control.

features.purpose: Scope the trail to an incident window
features.gap: Server-side filters exist (AuditLogController.php:121-126, validated at :31-32) and the service parameters exist; no control. This is the single most important missing filter for the stated compliance use case.
AuditLogController.php:115-117 supports actor_id and validates it at :29, but services/task/index.ts:160 does not even expose the parameter, let alone the UI.
Correctly distinguishes the two cases — one of the better-handled details in this unit.

Covers 8 of the ~23 slugs the backend emits. The 15 unmapped ones fall through to the raw slug: created, updated, schedule_updated, subtask_added, subtask_completed, subtask_reopened, subtask_removed, timer_started, timer_stopped, status_created, status_updated, status_deactivated, priority_created, priority_updated, priority_deactivated.

features.purpose: Name the subject of the change
features.reads: t.task_title LEFT JOIN, falling back to before.subject for config events
features.gap: The config-event fallback is a nice touch and works. But the title is not a link — from an audit finding there is no route to the task. And when a task is hard-deleted the LEFT JOIN yields null and the row degrades to 'Task #123'.

features.reads: actor name via LEFT JOIN tbluser (AuditLogController.php:105), created_at
features.shouldFeed: Organization/HRIT is the identity source and correctly supplies the actor name
features.gap: Falls back to 'System' when actor_id is null — but null actor arises from callers passing null (e.g. front_desk/taskController.php:906 when session user_id is absent), so 'System' can mean 'unattributed human action', which is exactly what an audit trail must not conflate.

Renders whatever five keys TaskAuditService.php:42-50 chose. There is NO after-state, so a 'Status changed' entry tells you the old status and leaves you to infer the new one. Raw column names are prettified only by replacing underscores (:143), so an auditor reads 'task allocated to: 412' rather than a person's name. For config events it renders 'subject: Status "In Review"', duplicating the title line above.
Configuration events are stored with task_id 0 (TaskAuditService.php:86), so every status/priority admin action renders a meaningless '#0' badge.
Shows the unfiltered total even while the client-side search box is narrowing the view — the numbers on screen disagree.
Correctly disabled at page 1; triggers a real refetch via the load dep at :61.
Server supports per_page; services/task/index.ts:160 does not expose it, so the page is fixed at the server default of 50 — which is also the ceiling of what the client-side search box can see.

features.purpose: Tell a compliance officer how long the trail is kept and that it cannot be edited
features.gap: No retention policy is stated or implemented; there is no purge job and no tamper-evidence. TaskAuditService writes are best-effort and swallow failures (:61-63, :92-94), so an audit row can be silently lost while the change it should have recorded succeeds — acceptable for telemetry, not for the 'compliance and security auditing' the customer specified.

features.element: Navigation registration for the five Administration screens
features.purpose: Route menu ids 217-221 to the right components
features.shouldFeed: Organization module owns the menu master and should give each row a distinct access_link
features.gap: Documented in the file itself: menu ids 217-221 all share the SAME access_link as id 215 ('/module/task-management/reports-and-analysis') in the live DB, so these five must match on submenuId instead and depend on a defensive fallback (normalizeTaskManagementAdministration in lib/gtg-navigation.ts). A backend data fix in tblmenumaster_g2g is outstanding; until then the Administration group's routing rests on a workaround.
